hero.title: Laser Levels System منظومات مستويات الليزر
hero.lead: Laser-generation systems are classified, according to the number of energy levels used, into a three-level system and a four-level system, which differ in the amount of pumping energy needed to achieve population inversion.

objectives: Explain how the three-level system works and how population inversion is achieved in it.
Explain how the four-level system works.
Justify why the four-level system is preferred over the three-level system in most laser devices.

content.heading: 💡 6-5 Laser Levels System منظومات مستويات الليزر

content.label: 📌 1- The Three-Level System
content.html: In this system there are three energy levels: the ground energy level (\(E_1\)), the intermediate energy level (\(E_2\)) — which is the metastable level — and the higher energy level (\(E_3\)) (excited level). See Figure 6-14.
extraHtml: When most atoms are in the ground energy level \(E_1\), the active medium is in a stable state; but when a suitable pumping technique is used, it will excite the active medium and move atoms from the ground level to the higher level \(E_3\). These atoms quickly drop from level \(E_3\) to level \(E_2\) (since the lifetime of level \(E_3\) is very short) — that is, the atoms' residence time in level \(E_2\) is shorter than the lifetime of level \(E_2\). Atoms thus accumulate in level \(E_2\) in numbers greater than in level \(E_1\), achieving population inversion between these two levels; the transition from level \(E_2\) to level \(E_1\) then generates the laser light.

content.label: 📌 2- The Four-Level System
content.html: This system involves four energy levels (\(E_1, E_2, E_3, E_4\)). See Figure 6-15.
extraHtml: Atoms of the system are pumped from the ground level (\(E_1\)) to the energy level (\(E_4\)), then the atoms rapidly decay from level (\(E_4\)) to the metastable level (\(E_3\)). Population inversion is then achieved between energy level (\(E_3\)) and energy level (\(E_2\)), generating the laser beam, even if the number of atoms in level (\(E_3\)) is small; because level (\(E_2\)) is nearly empty due to the rapid decay of atoms from it to level (\(E_1\)).
This means that this system requires less pumping energy to achieve population inversion compared with the three-level system.

questions.question: In the three-level system, the metastable level is:
questions.explain: In the three-level system, the intermediate energy level E₂ is the metastable level in which atoms accumulate.

questions.question: In the four-level system, population inversion is achieved between the two levels:
questions.explain: Population inversion is achieved between energy level E₃ (metastable) and energy level E₂, which is always nearly empty.

questions.question: Compared with the three-level system, the four-level system requires pumping energy that is:
questions.explain: The four-level system requires less pumping energy to achieve population inversion, because the lower level (E₂) is always nearly empty due to rapid decay from it.

summary.heading: 📋 Lesson Summary
items: The three-level system: E₁ (ground), E₂ (metastable), E₃ (excited). Pumping from E₁ to E₃, fast decay to E₂, laser from E₂ to E₁.
The four-level system: four levels E₁-E₄. Pumping from E₁ to E₄, fast decay to E₃, laser from E₃ to E₂, then fast decay from E₂ to E₁.
The four-level system requires less pumping energy to achieve population inversion, because the lower level of the laser transition (E₂) is always nearly empty.
